description: Clarkson’s first revival run moves from classical mythology and Cold War history through astronomy, Scottish landmarks and natural history, establishing a question ladder in which almost any corner of general knowledge can become suddenly expensive.

s01e01.description: Questions range from the humble spork and Tracey Emin’s My Bed to the BBC interview famously interrupted by children, the sirocco wind and Bates Motel. The ladder eventually reaches Greek mythology and Nike, the goddess of victory.

s01e02.description: Christopher Wren and St Paul’s, haggis and Burns, Heathrow’s airport code and Megatron all appear before the quiz wanders through Mount Fuji, Wagyu cattle, cilantro and Dave Brubeck, with the biblical Land of Nod among the stranger stops.

s01e03.description: Guy Fawkes, the wardrobe into Narnia, Blackpool Tower, Peter Rabbit and elephant-headed Ganesha share a question set that later travels into Cold War Berlin and Checkpoint Charlie. Chess pawns also manage to become relevant, because naturally they do.

s01e04.description: Harry Potter’s opening chapter, St Jude, bone china, Basil Fawlty, Greg Rutherford and Jamie Dornan all surface as the questions roam through religion, ceramics, comedy and sport. Geography eventually sends the ladder to the Balearic Islands.

s01e05.description: Turkish delight, Rodin’s The Kiss, Beaver Scouts, The Lion King, Kingston in Jamaica, snooker’s black ball and the RAF centenary all appear before astronomy turns the discussion heliocentric. An admirably disorderly tour from sweets to the Solar System.

s01e06.description: Chicken Run, Royal Dutch Shell and the gondola beneath an airship lead into Loch Ness and Urquhart Castle. The British Museum’s Hans Sloane origins and BBC Sports Personality also appear, giving the episode a particularly British mixture of engineering, history and trivia.

s01e07.description: A walkover in sport, New Zealand’s All Blacks, hula hoops, Charlie Bucket, Doctor Who, Theresa May’s prank P45 and acceleration all pass through the hot seat. Natural history contributes the ibex, a rather more sure-footed creature than most quiz reasoning.
